A great wyrm hangs frozen mid-dive above the keep, its jaws yawning open as a torrent of white-gold fire cascades across the eastern battlements — stone glowing molten at the impact — while armored defenders scatter like ants along the parapet walk far below.

The siege gate buckles at the exact instant a dozen battering-ram crews heave in unison, iron-banded oak splintering inward in a fan of shards, while ten thousand infantry press behind scaling-ladders already cresting the curtain wall on every side.

A coronation ring of heralds and lords crowds the great stair as the sovereign kneels at its summit, the crown descending finger-width from the archbishop's hands, banners of every noble house snapping taut in sudden wind, the assembled host below reduced to a dense jeweled carpet.

Three catapults release simultaneously, their payloads — boulders wreathed in alchemist's fire — frozen mid-arc above the outer ward, trailing smoke contrails, while the defending garrison on the ramparts raises shields in a single collective motion, tiny as beetles against the castle's face.

A leyline-rift tears open directly above the keep's highest spire, a vertical wound of violet-white light wide enough to swallow the tower entire, its edges fraying into branching arcs that rake the surrounding walls while mages on the battlements brace against the shockwave.

A hundred longships round the sea-cliff headland simultaneously, every oar-bank lifted in the turning stroke, prows aimed at the sea-keep's harbor gate, while signal fires ignite along the castle's coastal wall and the garrison's tiny silhouettes flood the sea-facing ramparts.

The north tower's upper third hangs suspended in the precise instant before gravity claims it — a siege-engine stone buried in its face, cracks flowering outward in every direction — while soldiers on the adjacent wall sprint away and the courtyard below empties in a rushing tide of figures.

A mage-circle of seven robed figures stands atop the tallest tower, arms raised, a summoning storm forming directly overhead: a churning column of lightning and dark cloud anchored to their circle, its base no wider than the tower-top, its crown spreading across the entire sky above the castle.

Cavalry five thousand strong crests the ridge above the castle's approach road in a single surging wave, lances leveled, morning sun catching ten thousand points of steel simultaneously, while the siege army below the walls turns in fragmented panic, tiny figures scattering from the thundering line.

A blood-moon eclipse locks into totality directly above the castle, the moon's copper-red disc perfectly framed between the two highest towers, its ruddy light flooding every courtyard and wall-walk with arterial color while pilgrims pressed against the outer gate stare upward in a single frozen gesture.

A mounted host of a hundred knights thunders through the castle's barbican gate in tight formation, the leaders already in the courtyard as the rearmost clear the portcullis, hooves scattering cobblestones, pennants horizontal in the rush of passage, stable-hands and squires flattening against the ward walls.

The coronation processional crosses the great stone bridge at its midpoint — the carriage flanked by mounted household knights, the bridge crowded rail-to-rail with cheering subjects — while on the castle's grand stair ahead, the full court waits in ranked tiers, the open doors of the throne-hall blazing with torchlight.

A summoning portal blooms in the courtyard center, a disc of emerald and gold fifty feet across, its surface rippling like struck water, already showing a shadowed landscape beyond, while knights ring it with raised weapons and court mages at its perimeter strain against the vortex pulling at their robes.

Two dragons wheel in opposite directions above the keep simultaneously, one banking left across the gatehouse trailing a veil of smoke, one diving right toward the great hall roof, their wingspans bracketing the entire castle between them, defenders on every wall frozen mid-action in the shadow of both beasts.

An aurora-storm envelops the upper towers in cascading curtains of jade and silver light, the spires visible as dark silhouettes within the radiance, while on the outer walls sentries have abandoned their posts and pressed together in clusters, tiny dark figures watching the castle's pinnacles burn with cold fire.

A siege army of forty thousand fills the plain before the gates from tree-line to tree-line, their banners raised, ranked formations locked in final dress before the assault order, siege towers and catapults positioned — frozen in the last breath of stillness — while the castle's walls bristle with every defender it holds.

The sky-tear above the outer gate has opened wide enough to frame a sky of alien constellations beyond, its edges crawling with silver runes, and through it the vanguard of an armed host is mid-step across the threshold, armored figures emerging into the castle's world while the gatehouse garrison falls back.

A dragon lands on the gate-tower at the exact moment its forelimbs grip the parapet, wingbeats throwing men from the wall-walk in every direction, tail sweeping across the outer face of the tower, the portcullis chains snapping under the impact, the beast's head level with the tower's signal-fire beacon.

The breach in the outer wall erupts at its peak: a magical impact strike has punched through thirty feet of dressed stone, the rubble expanding outward in a frozen cone of shards, dust-cloud blooming beyond the walls while infantry on both sides — tiny against the gap — are mid-lurch in every direction.

The great army assembles on the muster-plain below the castle's landward face: banners of a hundred lords planted in ranked order, cavalry formed in wings left and right, pike-blocks filling the center, all in the last moment before the warlord's signal — the entire host stretched from castle-shadow to the distant forest edge.

A leyline-storm cracks apart the sky above the keep, six forking columns of white energy striking the six highest spires simultaneously, the towers' capstones glowing incandescent at each impact point, while every figure on every battlement — guards, mages, archers — is thrown flat by the concussive wave radiating outward.

Knights-to-be kneel in a double rank across the castle's inner courtyard, swords planted before each one, the lord-commander moving along the line with the accolade blade, frozen at the moment it touches the shoulder of the tenth candidate — while behind them the entire garrison and household pack the courtyard walls, watching.

A colossal wyrm hangs suspended above the gatehouse, jaw stretched wide, a column of white-hot fire mid-pour across the barbican's crown — the stone already glowing orange and crumbling at the edges. Tiny knights scatter along the wall-walk below, cloaks ablaze, too small against the vast scaled belly overhead to be anything but doomed.

The sky above the inner courtyard tears open in a blinding violet rift sixty feet across, its churning rim spitting arcs of raw leyline energy against the surrounding towers. Hundreds of pilgrims packed into the courtyard below recoil as one, their upturned faces no larger than coins against the howling aperture above.

Three siege towers have reached the eastern curtain wall simultaneously — the lead tower's drawbridge crashing down onto the battlements at this very instant, the first wave of scaling men spilling onto the parapet. Below, a battering ram the size of an oak swings at the gate, ropes taut, scores of soldiers straining at its handles.

The king stands on the topmost step of the great ceremonial stair, crown inches above his bowed head, the high-lord's hands trembling at the apex of the gesture. A thousand subjects fill the entire approach bridge and courtyard below, their collective roar frozen in the air, banners snapping rigid in the wind above the packed, tiny multitude.

A thousand mounted knights crest the ridge above the castle's approach road at full gallop, lances leveled, the front rank already thundering down the slope toward the besieged gatehouse. From the ramparts, defenders the size of insects watch the vast tide of horseflesh and steel break over the hillcrest like a wave.
